notes: MITRE operates CWE, the canonical weakness taxonomy referenced by virtually all vulnerability databases. CWE provides a hierarchical classification of software and hardware weaknesses — views (organize by perspective), categories (group related weaknesses), and specific weakness entries. Over 900 weakness types. AI/ML weaknesses added in the CWE-1400 series. Referenced by CVE, NVD, and most vulnerability databases globally.

data.description: The canonical software and hardware weakness taxonomy, operated by MITRE.
data.notes:
CWE catalogs contain weaknesses, categories (renamed groupings in 5.0), and views. CWE 5.0 has 1,477 entries: 984 weaknesses, 431 groupings and 62 views. CWE-1448 is Weaknesses Related to AI/ML Products, introduced in 4.20. CWE-1425 is the 2023 CWE Top 25 Most Dangerous Software Weaknesses view.

Bare identifiers and unversioned subpaths accept case-insensitive CWE prefixes and use current HTML/API endpoints. The API reported ContentVersion 4.21 on 2026-11-18 and still uses /category/ for groupings. Explicit @versions select only entries present in the official archive for that release, with XML extraction instructions; live HTML/API endpoints are not historical snapshots.

Registered item membership covers 4.19, 4.19.1, 4.20, 4.21 and 5.0. Earlier releases remain available from MITRE’s archive index but are not registered for item resolution here. Membership and endpoint patterns are generated by scripts/sync-cwe.py from the reviewed, SHA-256-pinned release manifest.

urls.note: Official live MITRE CWE REST API; ContentVersion 4.21 verified 2026-11-18. Uses /weakness/, /category/, /view/ and universal entry-type lookup /cwe/{ids}. No release-selection parameter is documented.
